questions_and_answers.question_text: When is dōu used, even though "both" or "all" would not be used in English?
What is the difference between a collective and a distributive use?
What happens to the basic High tones of yī, qī, and bā before Falling-tone words?
Give three examples of the Falling-tone words that trigger this change.
What happens to the tones of 1, 7, and 8 in the digit-by-digit form of a year?
When is the tone change on yī, qī, and bā most common?

answers.answer_text: When the complete number given has only one digit.

questions_and_answers.question_text: With two or more digits, which are more likely to have Rising tones — the qī and bā of numbers ending in 7 and 8, or the yī of numbers ending in 1?

answers.answer_text: The qī and bā are more likely to have Rising tones; the yī of numbers ending in 1 is usually in the High tone.

questions_and_answers.question_text: In what kind of speech is the High tone more likely to be kept?
Write the Chinese for "One is nine, and one is six."

answers.answer_text: Yíge jiǔsuì le, yíge liùsuì le.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write 1986 in Chinese as a year.

articles.text:
10. A: Nǐmen nánháizi dōu jǐsuì le?         How old are your boys?
    B: Yíge jiǔsuì le, yíge liùsuì le.      One is nine, and one is six.

Notes on No. 10

The word dōu is used when "both" or "all" would probably not be used in English, namely, when expecting different information about each of the things (or persons) being discussed. "All" tends to be collective, asking or telling about something the members of a group have in common. Dōu can be distributive, asking or telling something about the members of a group as individuals.

yī, qī, bā: In the spoken language of Peking, the basic High tones of yī, qī, and bā usually change to Rising tones before Falling-tone words (such as -hào, yuè, and -suì). This change is most common when the complete number given has only one digit. When there are two or more digits, the qī and bā of numbers ending in 7 and 8 are more likely to have Rising tones than the yī of numbers ending in 1 (which is usually in the High tone). Compare:

Shíqīhào          the 17th
Shíyīyuè          November

In all cases, the High tone is more likely to be kept in rapid speech. You may also encounter speakers who never make changes in the tones of yī, qī, and bā.

Remember that, in the digit-by-digit form of giving the year, the numbers 1, 7, and 8 keep their basic High tones: Yījiǔbāliùnián, 1986
